content.value_statement: Teams often ship through pipelines that lack clear gates, rollback plans, or production checks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to design staged deployment workflows with approvals, strategies, and verification.
actual_capabilities: Maps standard CI/CD stages from source checkout through production verification.
Explains manual, time-based, and multi-approver deployment gate patterns.
Compares rolling, blue-green, canary, and feature flag rollout strategies.
Provides example patterns for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure Pipelines, and Kubernetes.
Covers rollback planning, health checks, monitoring metrics, and deployment success measures.
limitations: It provides design guidance and examples, not a running pipeline generator.
It does not validate platform permissions, secrets, or cluster access.
Example commands and URLs must be replaced before production use.
It does not replace incident response, compliance, or change management review.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Release Pipeline
use_cases.description: Create a staged path from build to production with tests, gates, verification, and rollback responsibilities.

use_cases.title: Improve Production Approvals
use_cases.description: Define approval gates, required reviewers, timing rules, and evidence checks before production deployment.

use_cases.title: Choose a Deployment Strategy
use_cases.description: Compare rolling, blue-green, canary, and feature flag approaches for a service risk profile.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Basic Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a single web service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a basic CI/CD pipeline for my web service. Include build, test, staging, approval, production, verification, and rollback stages.

prompt_templates.title: Add Approval Gates
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate release control for production changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design production approval gates for my deployment pipeline. Include reviewer roles, required checks, timing rules, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Select a Rollout Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced deployment planning for a higher-risk service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare rolling, blue-green, canary, and feature flag deployment strategies for my service. Recommend one strategy and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Architect a GitOps Release System
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced end-to-end pipeline design across environments.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GitOps deployment pipeline for multiple environments. Include security scans, approvals, progressive delivery, monitoring checks, and rollback automation.

output_examples.input: A startup needs its first production deployment pipeline for a web service.
output_examples.output: A staged release plan with source, build, test, staging, approval, production, verification, and rollback responsibilities.

output_examples.input: A team wants safer production releases after failed manual deployments.
output_examples.output: An approval workflow with reviewer roles, staging evidence, health checks, automatic rollback triggers, and clear recovery steps.

output_examples.input: An enterprise platform team needs a progressive delivery model for Kubernetes.
output_examples.output: A deployment strategy recommendation that compares rollout options, traffic shifting, monitoring gates, and operational tradeoffs.

best_practices: Start with fast tests and security checks before expensive deployment stages.
Require explicit production approval with clear evidence from staging and monitoring.
Define rollback criteria before deployment and test the recovery path regularly.
anti_patterns: Deploying directly to production without staging verification or approval.
Using one pipeline design for every service without considering risk.
Treating monitoring and rollback as manual tasks after a release fails.

faq.question: Does this skill create pipeline files automatically?
faq.answer: It provides architecture guidance and examples. Users must adapt the output to their platform and repository.

faq.question: Which CI/CD platforms does it cover?
faq.answer: It includes patterns for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure Pipelines, Kubernetes, and GitOps-style workflows.

faq.question: Can it help choose between canary and blue-green deployments?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains strategy tradeoffs and helps select a rollout model based on service risk.

faq.question: Does it handle secrets management?
faq.answer: It recommends using secret stores and secret references, but it does not configure secrets directly.

faq.question: Is it useful for compliance-heavy releases?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure approval gates and evidence checks, but compliance teams must review final controls.

faq.question: Can it design rollback steps?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers automatic and manual rollback patterns with health checks and failure criteria.
